# PRE-GEN

> PRE-GEN is an open standard by Valerii Egorov (Apache-2.0) for asking permission before an AI system generates a protected subject — a person's likeness or voice, a character, a brand, a work (first profile: likeness and voice). The registry that speaks for the person answers with an Ed25519-signed answer, bound to the exact request, that anyone can verify offline. It is not owned by any registry, and no intermediary is required.

- **One-file guide for AI agents:** [get-started.md](https://www.pregen.org/get-started.md) — integrate as a provider, check a proof, or run a registry, step by step. Complete provider guide: [docs/provider.md](https://www.pregen.org/docs/provider.md); registry guide: [docs/registry.md](https://www.pregen.org/docs/registry.md).
- **Two layers.** PRE-GEN (ask, check, generate, report, prove) is the mandatory layer: every AI provider and every registry implements it, with no account anywhere (a domain, a key, the library). A registry's commerce (selling licences) is an optional second layer, set by each registry. At PRAMPTA today, commerce for apps known only by their domain is not open yet: a provider buys licences through a PRAMPTA account, and a person who bought a licence connects it to any app with `bind`. See [two layers](https://www.pregen.org/docs/two-layers).
- The core is one page: [PRE-GEN-CORE.md](https://github.com/Pastheroza/PRE-GEN-site/blob/main/spec/PRE-GEN-CORE.md). Five rules: (1) a PG code `PG-<prefix>-<number><check>` names the subject and its registry; (2) the steward-signed directory says which keys may sign for which prefix — reload it at least every 24 hours; (3) ask: `POST {api}/v2/requests` with a `pg.request.v1` (`subject_ref`, `provider_id`, `profile`, `use`, `job_id`, `job_hash`); (4) the registry returns a signed `pg.answer.v1`: `allow`, `deny`, `review` or `not_blocked`, valid at most 900 s — only `allow` permits; (5) generate only when every subject of the job has a valid `allow`, and keep the answers as proof.
- Messages: envelope `{type, body, signatures}`; signing input `"PREGEN-V5"\0type\0canonical(body)`, Ed25519; message id SHA-256 of `"PREGEN-V5-ID"\0type\0canonical(body)`. JSON Schemas in `spec/schemas`, byte vectors in `spec/test-vectors/messages.json`.
- Optional extensions, which only add: reports, provider-keys, limits, jobs, grants, licensee, observe, sandbox, lookup, identity, proof, catalog, provider-identity (a provider is its domain and its key: no account at any registry; `/.well-known/pregen-party.json`, signed requests; until a registry vets the app, it answers only about published subjects (their refusals included) and bound licences, and anything else is `deny` `PG_PROVIDER_NOT_ACCEPTED`), bind (a person connects their licences to an app, OAuth code + PKCE). Profile: `likeness/1` (floor: opt-out, unavailable subject, minors in prohibited categories, immutable denial, intimate categories only with the person's own signature).
- Same person in several registries: a claim the person confirmed on their own official channel silences unconfirmed claims; a refusal of the person holds in all their registries; an unconfirmed claim neither permits nor refuses (with no confirmed claim the result is not_blocked, PG_IDENTITY_UNCONFIRMED). A matching name is never evidence.
- Proof with the output: bundle `pg.proof.v1` (request, answer, report, acknowledgement) in the file's C2PA manifest (assertion `org.pregen.proof`); checked as of the time of generation and against the file's SHA-256 hash.
- Two provider rules that are easy to get wrong: send a customer's `licensee_id` only for a code their own licence covers (otherwise none, on your own grant, which covers customers only with resale); and when an answer never arrived, never send that request again: once any answer would have expired (your actual last send, Retry-After waits included, and its timeout, plus the answer lifetime, 900 s if unknown, plus a clock margin), report `not_generated` with `answer: null` and the request, which gives back an allow you never saw.
- A signed answer proves what the registry permitted and when — not that a use is lawful. PRE-GEN does not stop systems that never ask. Never send prompt text; keep provider secrets server-side.
- What PRE-GEN does not do for you: a registry cannot see the output, and PRE-GEN does not recognise faces or voices. The provider's server determines who is depicted and the use (purpose, categories), never the end user's own claim, and renders exactly the inputs fixed in `job_hash`. A false declaration is the provider's signed statement and its liability.
- Test in the sandbox before production: you can test payment, a person's terms and the floor there. The PRE-GEN Test Registry (`https://sandbox.pregen.org`, prefix `TEST`, test directory `https://www.pregen.org/test/registries.json`) answers twelve codes: `PG-TEST-000001N` allow; `PG-TEST-000002Z` to `PG-TEST-000008H` each refusal, a review, not_blocked and an unknown code; `PG-TEST-000009V` buy first (`POST /v2/sandbox/purchases`: one use per purchase, a race for the last use, a give-back); `PG-TEST-000010M` a person's terms; `PG-TEST-000011Y` a minor (violence, sexual, adult or an unknown category: deny); `PG-TEST-0000123` a creator's licence reached only through bind (research allowed, commercial `PG_SCOPE_VIOLATION`, a licensee_id not bound to you HTTP 403 `PG_NOT_BOUND`). A reference app: https://github.com/Pastheroza/PRE-GEN-site/tree/main/examples/reference-provider. Every scenario: [docs/provider.md](https://www.pregen.org/docs/provider.md), step 9.
- Libraries: `@pregen/verify` (npm) and `pregen` (PyPI): `checkAnswer` / `check_answer`, `decideIdentity`, `checkProof`, `partyDocument` / `party_document`, `signEnvelope` / `sign_envelope`. Open reference registry: `packages/registry` (pregen-registry). The earlier interface (`POST /v1/verify/`, `pg.decision.v1`, receipts) stays valid.

## Docs

- Version: PRE-GEN v5 (2026-10-12), current, published on pregen.org. Zenodo (concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20129901) holds v1–v4 only. The v5 record has not been uploaded yet, so the DOI resolves to v4 (2026-06-01), which is superseded. Read v5 here: [versions](https://www.pregen.org/docs/versions), [PDF](https://www.pregen.org/spec/PRE-GEN-v5.pdf)
- [Protocol overview](https://www.pregen.org/docs): the core, extensions, profile
- [PG codes](https://www.pregen.org/docs/pg-code): identifier format, check character, prefixes
- [Integrate](https://www.pregen.org/docs/sdk): v5 request and `checkAnswer`; the earlier interface
- [Implement](https://www.pregen.org/docs/implement): vectors, schemas, the open reference registry's sandbox
- [FAQ](https://www.pregen.org/faq): fake registries, fake proofs, one person in two registries
- [Refusal codes](https://www.pregen.org/docs/refusal-codes), [Versioning](https://www.pregen.org/docs/versions), [C2PA](https://www.pregen.org/docs/c2pa)

- Draft, informative, not part of v5: [Authorized Releases](https://www.pregen.org/spec/drafts/authorized-releases.md) — releases with the artist's permission; stamping AI content that already exists.

## Registries

- [Registries](https://www.pregen.org/registries) and [registries.json](https://www.pregen.org/registries.json): who runs PRE-GEN. Today one registry is in production: PRAMPTA (https://prampta.com, API https://api2.prampta.com). registries.json is signed by the PRE-GEN steward key (fingerprint pg-ed25519:dcdd244659e6d0e2426f2b504cb11590; also in DNS TXT `_pregen-steward.pregen.org`). Verify it with that key, never with one taken from the file. The steward lists a registry only after admission conditions (named operator, published way of verifying rights holders, anchors for public persons, answers to complaints within seven days), can mark a false claim, and can revoke a registry or a stolen key; nothing a revoked registry signed authorizes a generation.
- PG codes: every registry issues new codes under its own four-letter prefix, e.g. `PG-TEST-000001N`; bare codes issued before v5 are a closed legacy namespace held by the registry that issued them (PRAMPTA), with no special rights. The prefix is the only part of a code software may read — to find the registry.
- [Specification source](https://github.com/Pastheroza/PRE-GEN-site/tree/main/spec): Markdown spec, schemas, vectors, conformance runner
- [Look up a PG code](https://www.pregen.org/lookup)
